task: Find the IDP and sign in
story: As an Application Developer, I want to sign in to the IDP with my corporate SSO, so that I do not need a separate credential to get started.
reasoning: Foundational — every other dev story depends on auth. SSO removes credential friction on day 1.

task: Find the IDP and sign in
story: As an Application Developer, I want to land on a "what can I do here" home page after sign-in, so that I do not need a wiki to figure out the next step.
reasoning: Adoption driver — without a clear next-step UI, devs bounce back to the old workflow.

task: Find the IDP and sign in
story: As an Application Developer, I want a one-click onboarding tour the first time I sign in, so that I can skip the docs and try a sandbox immediately.
reasoning: Nice polish; lower urgency since S002 already covers the cold-start gap in PI 1.

story: As an Application Developer, I want my team membership auto-resolved from SSO group claims, so that I do not need to file a ticket to be added to my own team's workspace.
reasoning: Direct hit on the IT-bottleneck pattern the user is trying to escape.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want to override or correct team-workspace membership when SSO claims are stale, so that I am not blocked by an HR data lag.
outcome: Admin escape hatch for SSO drift
reasoning: Operational safety net; SSO will be the path in 95%+ of cases, but the lag case is real.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to pick a sandbox blueprint from a catalog (e.g., "Node + Postgres", "Python + Redis"), so that I do not start from a blank Terraform file.
reasoning: Without a catalog, sandbox creation is a Terraform homework assignment and adoption stalls.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to click "Create sandbox" and have a working env in under 5 minutes with no approval gate, so that I stop using my personal AWS account.
reasoning: THE headline PI-1 story — directly tests H1+H2. Large size reflects integration work across IaC, AWS account, and IDP UI.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want every sandbox blueprint to pre-apply default security policies (private VPC, encrypted EBS, scoped IAM), so that the permit-by-default model is still safe by default.
reasoning: The thing that makes permit-by-default defensible to the platform team — without this, the carve-out in Q4 falls apart.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to fork a blueprint and tweak it for my use case, so that my team's pattern can become a new template without filing a ticket.
reasoning: Enables long-tail use cases without growing the platform-team review queue.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want to promote a community-forked blueprint to "official" status with a review, so that good patterns are amplified without forcing a review on every fork.
reasoning: Quality-control on the catalog; downstream of S009.

task: Apply tags and metadata at creation
story: As an Application Developer, I want the env-creation form to pre-fill team and cost-center from my profile, so that I do not retype them on every env.
reasoning: Resolves Q2 — devs accept mandatory tagging because the form does the work for them.

task: Apply tags and metadata at creation
story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want team, cost-center, and env-type tags to be mandatory at creation (no skip path), so that every env is attributable in cost reports.
reasoning: The foundational control that makes a future $40K spike attributable in hours, not weeks. Cheap to implement.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to override a default policy (e.g., open a port to the internet for a demo) with a one-line justification, so that I am not blocked but the platform team has an audit trail.
reasoning: Concrete embodiment of the user's "permit by default with auditing" stance. Without it, S008 becomes a wall.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want a "high-risk policy" subset (e.g., wide-open S3 in prod, public RDS) that does block rather than just warn, so that the most expensive mistakes cannot happen via override.
reasoning: Tightens governance after PI 1 evidence; deliberately not in PI 1 per user stance.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to store and retrieve non-prod secrets in a self-service vault from my env, so that I stop copy-pasting credentials in Slack.
reasoning: Direct kill of a real (and well-known) security anti-pattern; both personas align (Q8).

story: As an Application Developer, I want the IDP to inject secrets into my env as environment variables or mounted files, so that I do not roll my own bootstrap.
reasoning: Pairs with S015; without injection, devs script around the vault and reintroduce the leak.

story: As an Application Developer, I want a list of internally-available managed services (DBs, queues, caches) I can attach to my env in one click, so that I do not file a ticket for a dev Postgres.
reasoning: Closes another ticket-flow loop; reach is broad (every team needs a dev DB).

story: As an Application Developer, I want to request a new shared service to be added to the catalog with a justification, so that the catalog grows from real demand.
reasoning: Process plumbing; lower urgency than the initial catalog.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to install arbitrary tools, container images, or libraries in my non-prod sandbox without a security review queue, so that I can try things.
reasoning: Direct resolution of Q5 conflict; the platform-team objection is acknowledged via S020 background scanning.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want a background SBOM/scan job to run on BYO non-prod workloads and surface findings on a dashboard, so that BYO is observable without being blocking.
reasoning: The compensating control that makes S019 acceptable to the platform team. Without it, the Q5 compromise collapses.

task: Push to staging without a ticket
story: As an Application Developer, I want to deploy my containerized app to staging from the IDP UI or CLI, so that I do not need a release-manager ticket for non-prod pushes.
reasoning: Closes the loop from sandbox to a shared staging env — without it, devs build but don't ship.

task: Push to staging without a ticket
story: As an Application Developer, I want my deploy to show me logs and a healthcheck result in the UI, so that I know whether it worked.
reasoning: Without this, the deploy is a black box and devs go back to SSH/CLI workflows.

task: Push to staging without a ticket
story: As an Application Developer, I want preview environments per pull request, so that reviewers can click a link instead of pulling my branch locally.
reasoning: High delight per dev; gated on PI 1 deploy + sandbox primitives being stable.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want prod deploys to require a documented approver from a configured list, so that the permit-by-default model does not leak into prod.
reasoning: Both personas align on the prod carve-out (Q6). Not in PI 1 only because PI 1 is non-prod-focused.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to submit a prod deploy request from the same UI as my staging deploys, so that the workflow feels continuous even though prod is gated.
reasoning: Adoption hygiene — devs should not learn two UIs for the same intent.

task: See my env cost and usage
story: As an Application Developer, I want to see my env's running cost in near-real time in the IDP UI, so that I notice if I left something expensive running.
reasoning: Directly tests H1 — visibility is the user's chosen alternative to a hard cap.

task: See my env cost and usage
story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want a project-wide spend dashboard with per-team and per-env breakdowns, so that the next $40K spike is attributable in hours, not weeks.
reasoning: THE platform-team risk-reduction story for PI 1 — what they get in exchange for the deferred approval queue.

task: See my env cost and usage
story: As an Application Developer, I want to receive a budget alert when my env's projected monthly cost crosses a configured threshold, so that I am the first to know I have a problem.
reasoning: The user's chosen alternative to hard caps (Q3). Cheap, high-leverage, validates H1.

story: As an Application Developer, I want to tear down my env in one click and confirm everything is destroyed, so that I do not leak resources after I am done.
reasoning: Symmetric to S007 — devs only trust spin-up if teardown also works cleanly. Also a key cost-control mechanism for PI 1.

story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want auto-expiry on sandbox envs after a configurable idle period with a developer-controlled extension, so that forgotten envs do not accumulate.
reasoning: Strong cost-control lever once PI 1 telemetry shows the long-tail-leak pattern; not blocking for PI 1.

task: Audit trail for the platform team
story: As a Platform Team Engineer, I want every env creation, override, secret access, and deploy event logged to a queryable audit store, so that I can investigate incidents without paging the developer.
reasoning: Other half of the user's "permit by default with auditing" stance — without the audit trail, the model is just "permit by default".

task: Governance hardening (deferred per VP Eng stance)

reasoning: Conditional on evidence; deliberately downstream so the platform-team objection is addressable but not pre-committed.

story: IDP itself has SLO + on-call rotation
reasoning: Once PI 1 ships and devs depend on the IDP, IDP-itself outages become a Sev-2 issue.

story: Blueprint provisioning has retry/idempotency so a half-created env does not strand resources
reasoning: Cost-control AND reliability win — half-created envs are exactly how the $40K spike happens silently.

reasoning: Premature until adoption proves the IDP is critical-path.

reasoning: Pairs with S024 — once prod deploys are gated, prod secrets need the same gating.

reasoning: Operationalizes the BYO scanning compromise (S020); without an escalation policy the dashboard becomes write-only.

reasoning: Compliance lift; meaningful only after audit data has accumulated.
